value.0: It's done, then. The forge answers to iron again, and every robe on this rock has to wonder if the spear behind them learned from you. Rule the last: a doctrine is only clean while someone keeps it clean. That's you now. Go be inconvenient to sorcerers.

You smell like ambition and half a training. No. I hunt people who bend the galaxy with a thought, and I do it with a length of iron and better timing. Until the spear has nothing left to teach you, you're bait, not a hunter. Come back finished.

Come to learn magic? Then keep walking, I don't sell it. I sell the answer to it. Somebody in the Korriban Forge Caverns is teaching my counters to the exact robed filth they were built against. Their adepts drill at the outer forges right now, getting comfortable. Rule one: reach ends ritual. Go remind them. Put down six of their adepts and bring me the Forcebane Forge Heat Ledger they keep by the crucibles. I want to know how big this rot is.

Then it's signed. Outer gate, six adepts, the Forcebane Forge Heat Ledger by the crucibles. Don't read it, don't sell it, bring it. And if a robe offers you a better arrangement down there, remember they're the reason this trade exists.

Rule one, and carve it somewhere you'll see it: reach ends ritual. A sorcerer needs a breath to call the storm down. A spear crosses four meters in less. Forcebane isn't mysticism, it's arithmetic with a point on the end. Timing, distance, iron. The forge decides whether your arithmetic holds when the other side cheats.

Under the quarry ridge on Korriban, past the old Sith excavations. The Forge Caverns were sealed after the last dig went wrong; the smiths cut their own way back in. The key I'll hand you when you sign on opens the outer gate. Past that gate, every hammer you hear belongs to somebody who'd rather you didn't leave.

Smiths who trained as soldiers and pray like Sith. The adepts fight in pairs and they don't break when the first one drops. Keep your point moving, kill the chanting ones first, and don't let the forge floor pick your footing for you.
The ledger's still by the crucibles and six adepts are still breathing. Numbers don't improve while you stand in front of me.
Forge-smoke on your coat and ash on your hands. Let's see it, then.

Look at these rosters. They're not training a class, they're training a market. Every name in here paid in Sith script. Clean work; the credits are yours. Rest the arm, you'll want it. This goes deeper.

The ledger named suppliers, and the suppliers explain the rest. Their specialists are folding my counter-forms into Sith metallurgy, tempering blades against the very moves I built. Rule two: test the iron, not the word. Go back down, put five specialists on the floor, and bring me the Forcebane Sith Tempering Matrix intact. I want to see with my own eyes what they've bound into it.

Good. The matrix will be racked at the tempering line, deep side of the forges. Pull it before the coals cool or the imprint fades and it's just an ugly box. Five specialists stand between. Make them a schedule, then keep it.

A quench-frame. You seat a blade in it while the alloy sets, and whatever the frame holds, the steel remembers. Mine held angles and timing. Theirs holds Sith alchemy, so the metal remembers hate instead. If that sounds like mysticism to you, it is, and that's exactly why I want it on my bench and not theirs.

That's the question with a knife in it. Somebody who drilled under me is standing down there in better robes, drawing my forms on their chalkboards. The ledger's rosters were student handwriting. I trained maybe a dozen people who could teach this. The matrix will tell me which one turned.

Specialists don't drill in pairs, they drill with an audience of apprentices who join in uninvited. Expect the fight you planned plus half of one you didn't. Kill the specialist first and the audience remembers other appointments.
Five specialists and a racked matrix, deep side of the tempering line. It doesn't walk to you.
That box under your arm is humming. Good sign. Worse sign for them.

There it is. My angles, scored into a Sith quench-frame like scripture. I'll burn the imprint out tonight. You're not a stranger anymore, so hear this plain: what's past the tempering line doesn't fight fair, and I'm going to ask you to go there anyway.

The deep forge has a warden. Big smith, wears a sigil struck from the first anvil, cracked the day the old dig went wrong. Every counter I ever taught, he's tempered into himself, plus whatever they pray to down there. Rule three: never duel a warden fairly. I hunted sorcerers for twenty years and never once alone. Bait, blade, and net. Three roles, three people. Bring two you'd trust with your spine, kill the warden, and bring me the Forcebane Cracked Anvil Sigil off his neck.

Then go recruit before you go hunting. I mean it. The last one who took the deep forge alone came back in a crate with his spear folded in half, and he was better than you are today. Warden dies, sigil comes home, all three of you walk out.

He was the first one the turncoat trained, and the best. The sigil says the deep forge answers to him: quench lines, apprentices, all of it. He's felt every form I teach coming since before you learned to hold a spear level. That's what different means. Nothing you do will surprise him. Do it anyway, in numbers.

Old crew doctrine. Bait draws the commitment, blade punishes it, net closes the door behind. One hunter is a duel, and a duel is a coin toss against something like him. Three is arithmetic again. I don't send coin tosses.

Past the tempering line the floor is slag channels and the light is whatever's burning. The warden likes it there because crowds don't follow. Be the crowd anyway. And if he offers to let your friends leave so long as you face him alone, that's not honor, that's him doing arithmetic too.
The warden still holds the deep forge, and that sigil still hangs on his neck. If you're waiting for him to age out of it, sit down, it'll be a while.
The hammering stopped two nights ago. The whole ridge noticed. That was you.

Ha. Look at it. Cracked, same as their whole enterprise should have been from the start. The deep forge is headless and the apprentices are already leaving, my watchers say. You and your two did what a company of Republic regulars wouldn't price. The circle that's left knows your name now. Good. Fear makes people sloppy.

Four overseers left. The turncoat's inner circle. They sign the schedules, clear the shipments, decide which robes get trained next season. Rule four: leave no circle standing, because a circle regrows from any arc of it. Kill all four. One of them carries the Forcebane Overseer's Clearance Token, the stamp that moves their blades off Korriban. Bring it to me and the whole export dies with the hand that signs it.

Then hunt them the way they'd hunt you. Pick the arc, break it, move before the circle closes. Schedules first if you can find them, the quartermaster keeps those close. Four dead overseers and one token. After that there's only him.

Two smiths, a quartermaster, and a duelist who thinks she's my equal. All four drilled under the turncoat, which means all four drilled under me, once removed. They know my forms the way you know your own signature. So don't write your signature down there. Write something new.

Every crate of tempered blades leaving that forge carries the token's stamp, and the buyers pay on the stamp, not the steel. Take the token and the trade is paper. Their buyers are Sith, and Sith don't forgive missed deliveries. I'm not just ending a school. I'm arranging its creditors.

Not one at a time, if they can help it. The circle fights as a set. Staggered, patient, the duelist floating loose to take whoever overextends. Bringing your two again wouldn't shame you. Four against one is their favorite arithmetic. Change the numbers.
Four overseers, one token, and a forge holding its breath. The circle doesn't disband because you got busy.
You're standing straighter. That's what killing a circle does. Show me.

Four names I trained, once removed, closed out in a week. The stamp still smells of ink. They were clearing a shipment when you arrived. That's the trade dead, the school headless, the buyers furious. All that's left is the man who taught them, and that one I have to talk about sitting down.

His name doesn't matter anymore. He traded it for a title. The master of that forge is the man I built this doctrine with. Thirty years of hunts, half my rules are his. Then he decided the counters were worth more sold than kept and turned the whole discipline inside out. He carries Forcebane the way you're trying to. The full weight of it, the guard that unmakes whatever touches it. And he knows the rule I'm about to give you, because he wrote it with me. Rule five: finish what you teach. Take your two, go to the heart of the forge, and put him down. No trophy this time. Him ended is the proof.
Then that's the last order I have in me. Heart of the forge, three of you, no duels. When it's done, come stand where you're standing now. I want to hear it plain, not through watchers.

My net-man. Bait, blade, and net, and he was the net, the one who closed doors. Best timing I ever hunted beside. When you face him, that's what you're fighting: every escape you'd use, already closed. He'll ask about me. Tell him I kept the rules. He'll know which one I mean.

You don't out-rule him. You out-number him, and you take the trade the numbers offer. He can end any one spear that comes at him. That's what mastery of this doctrine means. So don't send one spear. Three angles, no pauses, and no respect for the moment he creates where facing him alone feels right. That moment is his weapon. Refuse it.

The forge heart is his temple now. Heat that bends your sight, one bridge over the crucible, and him at the middle of it, patient as an anvil. Nobody walks off that bridge alone, so don't walk onto it alone. And he will talk. He talks better than I do. If your feet stop moving while he does, your friends are carrying you home.
He's still at the heart of the forge, and he knows the circle's gone. Men like him don't run. They set their feet and wait for the lesson to arrive. Go be the lesson.
The watchers went quiet, then came the smoke, then you, walking like a man with nothing left to prove. Say it anyway. I've earned hearing it.

Ours again. Yours, mostly, now. Thirty years I wondered if the rules were worth what they cost, and you answered it with his own doctrine turned back on him one last time. Forcebane is yours. Whole. The guard, the answer, the arithmetic. Rule the last, peer to peer: keep it sharper than your grudges. That's the one he broke.
Go over the job again.
Six adepts. One ledger. I'll get it done.
Why a spear against Force users?
How do I get into these caverns?
What's waiting in there besides adepts?
Not today.
The Forcebane Forge Heat Ledger. Six adepts stopped arguing about it.
Run the second job past me again.
Five specialists. I'll bring the matrix back whole.
What is a tempering matrix?
How did your counters end up on Korriban?
How do the specialists fight?
Give me a day first.
One Forcebane Sith Tempering Matrix, warm off the rack.
Tell me about the warden again.
I'll find two worth trusting. The warden falls.
What makes this warden different?
Why bait, blade, and net?
What's it like past the tempering line?
I need to find my two first.
The Forcebane Cracked Anvil Sigil. He didn't want to part with it.
Walk me through the circle again.
All four. And the token comes home.
Who are the four?
What does the token actually clear?
How will they come at me?
Let me sharpen up first.
The Forcebane Overseer's Clearance Token. The circle's signatures are done.
Tell me about him once more.
We'll finish it. All three of us.
What was he to you?
How do I beat the man who wrote the rules?
What happens at the heart of the forge?
Not yet. Not until we're ready.
It's finished. The master is dead, and the doctrine is yours again.
